explanations: broadcast iterates the room's member array directly, and when it finds a closed or too-slow connection it calls leaveAll, which splices that connection out of the same array. An array iterator walks by index, so after the splice every later member shifts down one place and the iterator steps over the one that moved into the removed slot. That watcher silently misses the event, and with consecutive slow clients some are neither sent to nor disconnected. Iterating over a snapshot ([...members]) lets the hub remove connections from the live array without disturbing the loop, so every remaining member is visited exactly once.
